newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania average one-week rate jumps to 426.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania average one-week rate jumps to 426.50 pct.

text.p: The average rate on one-week funds at the Romanian central bank (BNR) refinancing auction on Thursday soared to 426.50 percent from 226.35 last week as the BNR continued its tough monetary policy.

The BNR's one-week funds offer of 510 billion lei ($63.8 million), down from 520 billion lei last week, was heavily oversubscribed, with six banks bidding a total 1.79 trillion lei at rates ranging from 227 percent to 426.50 percent.
The Lombard rate, applied to overdraft credits and set by multiplying the average one-week auctioned rate by 1.6, is also expected to rise. It was previously set at 362.16 percent.
The central bank intends to use tighter monetary policies to fight surging inflation and boost confidence in the leu.

January inflation rose to 13.7 percent from December's 10.3 percent and is expected to quicken in coming months after fuel, electricity and food prices were liberalised this week. Interbank traders also said short-term rates, which hovered near 340 percent throughout the day, should rise on the back of the higher average one-week rate on a money market starved for the leu. The rise in the average one-week rate followed intervention on the foreign exchange market on Wednesday when traders said the BNR had sold "several million" dollars.
The leu closed on Thursday in interbank trading between 7,000/100 to 8,200/300. After intervention on Wednesday, it strengthened to 7,200/310 to 8,800/50 from its open of 8,200/300 to 8,900/9,000.
